name: Office tenant improvement
summary: Interior build-out of office space in an existing shell: partitions, ceilings, finishes, doors, millwork, distribution MEP and fire protection. Cost swings with density of enclosed offices, glass, millwork and MEP intensity; data quality is good (Cushman 42-city guide, Kirksey Texas surveys, Cumming metros, JLL).

typicalSize.method: Judgment for a single tenant suite; Kirksey benchmarks a 25,000-NRSF floor plate (e1).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Mid-range (standard) TI, construction only, per usable/rentable SF. Kirksey 2025 mid-range: Houston $107–140, Dallas $108–133, Austin $114–148 (avg midpoint ≈ $125, Texas ≈ 10–12% below national). Cushman 2026 U.S. city range $108–219 (e4) with the middle of the distribution ≈ $150–160. Cumming metro TI ranges (e8) are wider and higher ($150–450) because they cover higher-end fit-outs. Mid = $150 (Kirksey Texas ≈ $125 scaled to national ≈ $140, and Cushman mid ≈ $155). Low = $95 ≈ Kirksey basic/second-gen. High = $260 ≈ Kirksey higher-end midpoint and Cumming 10-metro median midpoint ($320) trimmed. Mixed 2025/2026 evidence expressed in 2026 dollars (≤1-year gap).

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC and fee; excludes AV/IT/security cabling and equipment, furniture, soft costs and landlord base-building work.

qualityTiers.method: Kirksey tier midpoints vs. mid-range midpoint (Houston/Dallas/Austin): basic ≈ $93–103 / $120–131 ≈ 0.75–0.8 (economy set to 0.65 to cover light second-gen refreshes); higher-end ≈ $219–238 / $120–131 ≈ 1.8 → premium 1.5, luxury 1.9.

systemSplit.method: Cushman NYC 2026 hard-cost trade breakdown (e6) with contingency ($20.41) removed: GC/fee $21.84 → 01 10.9%; millwork 6.6% → 06; doors/frames/hardware 10.7% → 08; drywall/acoustic/carpentry + general finishes $39.92 → 09 19.9%; misc. architectural 3.7% → 10; mechanical/plumbing/fire protection 25.1% split 23 18.6% / 22 4.0% / 21 2.5% (judgment); electrical 23.1% split 26 19.0% / 27 2.6% / 28 1.5% (judgment).

lineItems.name: First-generation space premium (no existing improvements)

cost.method: Kirksey 2025 mid-range: "Add up to" $17 (Houston), $22 (Dallas), $23 (Austin); basic tier $14–18. Low set at $8 (partial first-gen).

lineItems.notes: Turn on when building out a raw shell floor for the first time.

lineItems.name: Low-voltage cabling, AV and security

cost.method: Cushman NYC example: IT 4% + A/V 12% of hard = 16% (e5); JLL: security/IT/AV ≈ 10–12% of total fit-out (e10). 16% × $150 mid ≈ $24/SF; low ≈ 10% × $150; high ≈ 16% × $250.

lineItems.notes: Usually tenant/owner-direct, outside the GC contract.

cost.method: Derived judgment: light selective demo of partitions/ceilings/flooring in occupied-building conditions; no public source fetched.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Kirksey 2025 furniture $30–85 (Dallas) / $35–90 (Houston); mid-range $45–60 → mid $50. Cushman NYC furniture = 22% of hard ($48.54) corroborates.

pctOfHard.method: Cushman NYC example: soft costs 10% + misc 2% of hard (e5). Range widened for small projects (higher fixed design/permit costs) and project management fees.

softCosts.notes: Excludes moving costs and furniture (see ffe) and AV/IT (line item).

hard.method: Interior work in existing buildings carries unknowns; Cushman's NYC hard-cost build-up carries $20.41 contingency on $200.21 ≈ 10% (e6).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard + soft (excl. FF&E/AV): min ≈ $85 basic × 1.08; max ≈ Cumming Chicago high $450 (e8). JLL all-in (incl. furniture/AV) $230–375 (e7) sits inside.
